en.name: Garam masala
en.summary: Garam masala keeps 1 year in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard. It is a ground blend of warm spices, so it fades rather than spoils — a jar past its year smells faint rather than being unsafe.
en.pantry: 1 year in an airtight jar, cool, dark and away from the hob. Garam masala is built on cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper and cumin, usually toasted and then ground, and toasting is exactly what makes a fresh blend smell so good and then fade so noticeably: heat drives the aromatic oils to the surface, where the air can take them. Judge it by smell, not by the label. Warm a pinch in your palm; a good masala lifts immediately, a tired one smells of dust. Adding more of a faded blend does not recover the aroma, it just adds bulk.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for garam masala. A ground blend in a humid fridge cakes and takes on other smells, both of which cost more than the cold saves. Keep it in a sealed jar in a cupboard away from the cooker, which is what the published figure assumes. If you do chill it, let the jar reach room temperature before opening so condensation stays off the powder.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either, and the condensation problem is worse than in the fridge. The better answer is the traditional one: keep the whole spices — cardamom pods, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, cumin seed — and toast and grind a small batch every month or two. Whole spices outlast ground ones for the simple reason that less surface is exposed to air.
en.thawing: Not applicable — garam masala is a dry cupboard blend and should not be frozen.
spoilage: Little or no lift when you warm a pinch in your palm.
A flat, dusty smell rather than a sweet, warm one.
Caking into hard lumps, meaning moisture has got in.
Mould or a musty smell in a jar that got damp.
tips: Buy or make small quantities; a large tub will fade long before you finish it.
Keep the whole spices and grind fresh batches when you can.
Add it near the end of cooking, not at the beginning, to keep the aroma.
Use a dry spoon and never shake it over a steaming pan.

faq.q: How long does garam masala keep?
faq.a: 1 year in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard.
No. Ground spice blends fade rather than spoil. A faded jar makes a flatter dish; only a damp jar with mould should be thrown out.

faq.q: Should garam masala go in at the start or the end of cooking?
faq.a: Near the end. It is a finishing blend, and the aromatics it is made for are driven off by long cooking.

zh.name: 印度綜合香料（garam masala）
zh.summary: garam masala 裝在氣密罐、放陰涼避光的櫥櫃可放 1 年。它是溫暖系香料磨成的綜合粉，所以它是淡掉而不是腐敗——過了一年的罐子是香氣變弱，不是不安全。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼、避光、遠離爐台，1 年。garam masala 的骨架是小豆蔻、肉桂、丁香、黑胡椒與孜然，通常先烘香再磨；而「烘香」正是新鮮的配方聞起來那麼好、之後又退得那麼明顯的原因：加熱把芳香精油逼到表面，空氣就把它們帶走了。請用聞的判斷，不要看標籤。在手心搓熱一小撮：好的馬薩拉會立刻揚起來，累了的只剩灰塵味。退掉的配方加再多也救不回香氣，只是多了份量。
zh.fridge: garam masala 沒有公布的冷藏期限。研磨綜合香料放進潮濕的冰箱會結塊、也會吸別的味道，兩者的代價都比低溫省下來的多。請用密封罐放在遠離爐具的櫥櫃，那正是公布數字預設的條件。若真的冰過，請讓罐子回到室溫再打開，免得結露落在粉上。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據，而且結露問題比冷藏更嚴重。更好的答案是傳統做法：保留整粒香料——小豆蔻莢、肉桂、丁香、胡椒粒、孜然籽——每一兩個月烘香現磨一小批。整粒香料之所以比磨好的耐放，理由很單純：暴露在空氣中的表面比較少。
zh.thawing: 不適用——garam masala 是乾燥的櫥櫃綜合香料，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 在手心搓熱一小撮，幾乎沒有香氣揚起。
只剩平板的灰塵味，而不是甜暖的香氣。
結成硬塊，代表水氣跑進去了。
受潮的罐子長霉或有霉味。
tips: 買或做小份量；一大桶往往在你用完之前就先退掉了。
整粒香料留著，有空就現烘現磨一小批。
起鍋前才加，不要一開始就下，香氣才留得住。
用乾湯匙，也不要在冒蒸氣的鍋子上方抖罐子。

faq.a: 氣密罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，1 年。

faq.q: 放很久的 garam masala 有危險嗎？
faq.a: 沒有。研磨綜合香料是淡掉而不是腐敗。退掉的罐子只會讓菜變平淡；只有受潮發霉的才該丟。

faq.q: garam masala 該一開始下還是最後下？
faq.a: 接近起鍋時下。它是收尾用的香料，長時間加熱會把它的香氣趕光。
